articles.title: 打破全天候监听疑云：苹果详解 iPhone 18 Pro / Max 处理 Hey Siri 背后流程
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，苹果公司今天（11 月 12 日）发布新博文，详细介绍了面向 iPhone 18 Pro 等设备的全新“安全隔离区”（Secure Exclaves）架构，并详细介绍了“Hey Siri”背后的流程。根据官方博文内容，在 iPhone 18 Pro 和 iPhone 18 Pro Max 上，苹果为“Hey Siri”语音唤醒词设计了“先低功耗初筛、再隔离区复核、最后经屏幕指示校验后才放行音频”的流程，从而减少误唤醒，并让用户能直观看到设备何时真正开始收音。在运转流程方面，IT之家援引博文介绍，附上运转流程如下：常驻低功耗监听：Always-On Processor（AOP）持续监听环境声音，寻找可能是“Hey Siri”的语音片段。它只做粗略的第一轮判断，不会直接把完整录音交给主系统。疑似唤醒才唤醒主芯片：一旦 AOP 判定“可能听到了唤醒词”，iPhone 18 Pro 和 iPhone 18 Pro Max 才会唤醒主处理器，并把相关音频缓冲交给音频隔离区（audio exclave），这可以避免主芯片长期高功耗运行。音频隔离区先做回声消除：音频隔离区对音频执行回声消除等处理，让语音更清晰，再把处理后的音频交给 Siri 隔离区。第二道更精细的复核：Siri 隔离区运行更大、更精细的唤醒词识别模型，进一步确认用户是否真的说了“Hey Siri”。苹果称，这一步能过滤掉远多于 AOP 单独判断时的误报。确认后才“叫醒” Siri：若确认唤醒词成立，Siri 隔离区只向主系统中的 Siri 守护进程发送一个“唤醒”标志；此时并不向其传输音频。请求麦克风并显示指示点：Siri 守护进程随后向音频驱动请求麦克风权限，音频驱动则调用界面绘制麦克风指示点，并向“隔离区指示控制器”（EIC）申请音频访问。屏幕指示必须通过校验：EIC 会要求安全显示隔离区检查屏幕上渲染出的麦克风指示点，包括颜色、形状、显示时长、最低亮度，以及附近像素是否遮挡了它。只有校验通过，系统才会从“环境模式”切换为“主动模式”，并允许音频流出。音频才交给 Siri：校验通过后，Siri 隔离区才把包含“Hey Siri”的历史音频及后续请求内容交给 Siri 守护进程。指示点会持续显示到 Siri 会话结束，且最短持续 3 秒。iPhone 18 Pro、iPhone 18 Pro Max 为了随时响应“Hey Siri”，是不是一直在后台录音录像？对此苹果公司在博文中回应称，后台采用阅后即焚的处理机制，在常驻低功耗监听状态下，摄像头和麦克风捕捉到的原始画面和声音会被直接送入芯片上完全独立的 Secure Exclaves 隔离区。数据进入隔离区后，AI 只负责把复杂的音视频简化为极简的信号（比如“有人来了”、“这是家庭成员 A”、“听到了唤醒词”）。一旦识别完成，原始的音视频数据会立刻被销毁。而且苹果公司承诺“谁都拿不到原始数据”，不仅第三方 App 拿不到，就连 iOS / macOS 主系统，甚至苹果公司自己，都无法访问或提取隔离区里的原始音视频流。参考Secure Exclaves and Ambient Sensing

articles.title: 郭明錤谈黄仁勋出轨丑闻：他似乎很难全身而退，英伟达可能得布局接班计划了
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，香港天风国际证券分析师郭明錤今日在 X 平台发文，谈到近期发生的英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋出轨丑闻。郭明錤认为，黄仁勋对英伟达来说至关重要。因为他能把工程团队认为可能实现的技术，转化为全公司愿意投入资源、承担风险，而且必须交付的产品。正是这种能力，让供应链能有极高的订单能见度，并配合激进的规格升级。而这也带动了竞争对手的跟进，进一步推动整体 AI 产业技术升级与供应链投资。同时他表示，相比让供应链获得明确的订单预期，决定采用更激进的技术规格，并推动其真正落地，才是更困难的事情。黄仁勋可以不是英伟达最懂 HVDC（IT之家注：高压直流输电）、CPO（共同封装光学）/NPO（近封装光学）与 CCL（铜箔基板）/PTFE（聚四氟乙烯）等新技术的人。但他的真正价值，在于同时考虑策略、组织、技术与供应链，并迅速拍板定案与投入资源执行。此外这名分析师认为，从目前公开信息来看，黄仁勋似乎很难全身而退。在这种前提下比较务实的做法，可能是让英伟达阶段性降低黄仁勋个人的决策依赖，同时布局接班计划。在这过程中，英伟达能否延续高效新产品与技术研发，以及竞争对手如何回应，将是整体 AI 技术发展和投资趋势的重点。相关阅读：《网友喊话马斯克聘请黄仁勋，马斯克回应称“那将会是我的荣幸”》《黄仁勋遭美国议员要求辞职，英伟达面临国会问询压力》《桃色丑闻重创 AI 芯片巨头：黄仁勋第二段婚外情曝光，英伟达盘后股价重挫逾 9%》《英伟达董事会已聘请外部机构物色新 CEO 候选人以接替黄仁勋，同时考虑临时 CEO 方案》《消息称黄仁勋已回英伟达上班开会，试图表现得“一切照常”》《英伟达董事会聘请前美国联邦检察官，调查 CEO 黄仁勋相关事件》《身价 30 分钟缩水约 74 亿美元：英伟达黄仁勋陷婚外情风波，跌至全球富豪榜第十》《承认婚外情后，英伟达 CEO 黄仁勋退出 ElevenLabs 峰会等多项公开活动》《英伟达黄仁勋遭股东集体诉讼，出轨丑闻致公司市值蒸发超万亿元》《马斯克回应黄仁勋出轨风波，同意其对美国 AI 产业不可或缺》《英伟达黄仁勋承认出轨：“我对妻子不忠，伤害了家人，没有任何借口”》

articles.title: 百度天池 1024 卡超节点发布：可支撑 5 万亿参数模型训练，明年上市
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日现场消息，在今日举办的百度世界 2026 大会开幕式上，百度集团执行副总裁沈抖发布百度天池 1024 卡超节点，这套算力集群将于明年推向市场。百度天池 1024 卡超节点搭载业界领先光引擎技术，卡间互联带宽提升 3 倍，实现高速数据互联，对比上一代产品，训练性能提升 2.5 倍、推理性能提升 3 倍。百度天池 1024 卡超节点配套 G3.5 KV Cache 显存加速柜，强化缓存复用能力，长上下文推理性能提升 2 倍；在多轮对话缓存命中场景，TTFT（首 token 等待时间）降低 90%，整体吞吐提升 7 倍。单套天池 1024 卡超节点可支撑 5 万亿参数大模型训练，具备优秀的横向扩展能力，能够扩展至万卡规模集群。IT之家注意到，百度曾在去年的百度世界大会上宣布天池千卡级超节点 2028 年上市，如今节奏加快了一年。此外，昆仑芯 N 系列也提前到 2028 年发布。

articles.title: R 星入驻抖音，首条视频喊玩家马上预载《GTA6》
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，游戏开发商 RockstarGames 今日入驻抖音，认证信息显示为“ROCKSTAR INTERNATIONAL LIMITED”，IP 属地上海。目前 R 星已经发布他们的第一条抖音视频，为 11 月 19 日发售的《GTA6》游戏做宣传，视频内容是将昨天发布的预载宣传片进行重新剪辑，适配竖屏播放场景。官方称《Grand Theft Auto VI》现已开放预载，并呼吁玩家马上预载本作。IT之家注意到，此次入驻抖音并非 R 星第一次布局国内市场。早在 2023 年，R 星就已经开设B站账号，宣传《GTA》和《荒野大镖客》等系列游戏，当时的玩家们似乎并不关注视频内容，而是一致催更《GTA6》。

articles.title: 知情人士回应“腾讯裁员 50%”系谣言误读，该说法完全不属实
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，针对社交媒体上流传的“腾讯裁员 50%”“裁员 8000 人”等说法，接近腾讯的知情人士今日回应新浪科技称，相关传言系对内部讲话的误读，该说法完全不属实。这一传闻的起点是 11 月 11 日腾讯 28 周年司庆期间的 Linktime 线上直播。据上述知情人士描述，腾讯管理层在直播中表达了加快组织变革的决心，并用一组比喻解释资源重配的思路：公司业务基本盘是“陆军”，AI Native 业务是“海军”；“陆军”要借助 AI 提升效能，同时调整 50% 的人员转向“海军”，支持 AI Native 业务的探索。IT之家注：AI Native 指从产品设计之初就以 AI 能力为核心构建，而非在既有产品上叠加 AI 功能。这一表述在传播中被简化为“裁员 50%”，随后衍生出“8000 人”“职级 13 元老被裁”等多个版本。该知情人士强调，此轮变革与几年前那一次“降本增效”性质不同。前一次相对被动，重心偏向“降本”；本次是面向 AI 时代的主动出击，重心偏向“增效”—— 鼓励一线同事积极举手向前冲，中间管理层则需要变得更扁平和灵敏。其表述的框架是“50% 的人守土有责，50% 的人拥抱浪潮”，而非削减一半员工。在此之前，在 2026 年 5 月股东大会上，腾讯总裁刘炽平曾回应裁员问题时表示“肯定没有大裁员计划，腾讯跟硅谷公司不太一样”。截至目前，腾讯官方尚未就 11 月这轮传闻发布正式声明，知情人士的回应是目前可获得的最高层级澄清。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，科技媒体 CNET 本月针对美国市场销售的 32 款手机发布续航报告，称苹果 iPhone 18 Pro Max 成为综合续航表现最好的机型。在测试手机方面，该媒体在 2026 年共计测试 28 款新手机，不过该媒体还是收录了 4 款今年没有更新的机型，因此榜单上共有 32 款。在测试时间方面，该媒体对这些手机的总测试时长累计超过 120 小时。测试项目方面，该媒体的测试更倾向于掉电测试，包括以下两个项目：3 小时视频流媒体测试：在满电、屏幕最高亮度、Wi‑Fi 环境下连续播放视频 3 小时，记录剩余电量。45 分钟压力测试：满电状态下进行视频播放、视频通话、游戏、刷社交媒体等高强度操作，记录剩余电量。结果显示，iPhone 18 Pro Max 在 45 分钟压力测试中仅掉电 1%，与 iPhone Duo 并列第一；谷歌 Pixel 11 Pro XL 则以仅 3% 的耗电并列第三。在 3 小时视频测试中，iPhone 18 Pro 表现最佳，仅消耗 6% 电量。CNET 认为，iPhone 18 Pro Max 胜出得益于更大的电池容量、iOS 27 的系统优化以及 A20 Pro 芯片的能效提升。IT之家附上相关图片如下：值得注意的是，电池容量大并不必然等于续航久。测试显示，更亮的屏幕、更强的处理器以及 AI 功能都在消耗新增电量，因此 2026 年新机的平均续航与 2024 年、2025 年机型基本持平。硅碳电池成为本年度最受关注的技术变化。摩托罗拉 Razr（2026）和三星 Galaxy Z Fold 8 等折叠屏手机已开始采用这种电池，它能在不显著增大电池体积的情况下提升容量。CNET 预计，2027 年及以后将有更多厂商采用该技术。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日现场消息，在今日（11 月 12 日）举办的百度世界 2026 开幕式上，百度创始人李彦宏在谈及 AI 芯片时表示，过去 AI 算力需求主要以训练为主，而现在是训练与推理并重的格局，尤其是智能体应用的规模化，带动了推理计算需求的大爆发。“我们相信，推理将成为 AI 芯片长期持续增长的主要推动力。”IT之家在大会现场了解到，昆仑芯介绍了下一步产品计划。目前 M100 已如期上市，M300 将于明年推出。其中，M100 主打极致性价比；而作为旗舰款 M300，则在算力、存储、互联等多个维度，实现了全方位能力跃升。到 2028 年，基于全新 N 架构的多颗芯片也将推向市场，精准匹配差异化应用场景。李彦宏说，百度一直是一家相信技术、并愿意长期投入的公司。“昆仑芯就是我们十多年坚持投入的结果，它的商业价值正获得越来越广泛的认可。”

articles.title: 演员赵丽颖起诉红果短剧侵犯肖像权
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，据南华视频报道，红果短剧的运营主体 —— 北京笔墨留香科技有限公司新增开庭公告，案由涉及肖像权纠纷，原告方为赵丽颖，被告方为北京抖音信息服务有限公司、北京笔墨留香科技有限公司、史某伦。开庭法院为北京市门头沟区人民法院云法庭，开庭时间为 2026 年 11 月 10 日。北京笔墨留香科技有限公司成立于 2021 年 7 月，注册资本 100 万元，经营范围包含广播电视节目制作、电视剧制作、互联网信息服务、电影发行等，由北京抖音信息服务有限公司全资持股，旗下产品为红果短剧 App。IT之家注意到，网传多家报道提及索赔 81 万元，但该金额存在口径分歧，有媒体指出该金额可能对应另一起侵权案，本次开庭公告未明确披露具体索赔信息。早在 2021 年，赵丽颖、杨幂等 514 位行业人士就曾联合发布《倡议书》，称只有对影视作品内容进行有效的版权保护，才能让行业生生不息。红果短剧创作者中心 11 月 9 日发布的《AI 剧虚拟形象创编与确权能力上线公告》指出，在 AI 剧虚拟形象创作中，形象可能来源于真人授权、上游 IP 授权或原创创作，涉及肖像、美术设计等多类权益。为帮助各位创作者前置上传权属材料，避免后续发布作品受到影响，平台现提供“虚拟形象创编与确权”能力支持。

articles.title: Mac 版 ChatGPT 新增“财务”入口：让 AI 替你管账、查消费、盯投资
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，OpenAI 今天（11 月 12 日）在 X 平台发布推文，宣布 ChatGPT Finances 功能正式扩展至 Mac 桌面应用。用户更新 ChatGPT 应用后，即可在侧边栏的“财务”入口连接银行、信用卡及投资账户，直接在 macOS 上查看余额、分析消费、管理订阅并跟踪投资组合。该功能通过金融数据服务商 Plaid 接入账户，ChatGPT 可基于真实交易、余额和投资数据回答问题。例如，用户可以直接询问“这个月我在哪儿花钱最多？”或“哪些订阅应该取消？”，AI 会结合账户信息给出个性化分析。IT之家附上相关截图如下：ChatGPT Finances 于今年 5 月上线，其主要卖点是按类别追踪支出并寻找省钱空间、审查定期扣费和即将到期账单、监控股票持仓与资产配置、跟踪信用评分及影响因素，以及生成每周财务动态。用户还可设置储蓄目标、评估还债方案，并使用语音对话、股票观察列表和自定义财务工具。隐私方面，OpenAI 强调该连接为“只读”权限：ChatGPT 不能转账、支付账单或执行股票交易，用户也可随时断开账户连接。

articles.title: 英 AI 芯片初创企业 Fractile 获该国政府资金支持，估值达 70 亿美元
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，英国人工智能芯片初创企业 Fractile 当地时间昨日宣布完成了超 7.2 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 48.14 亿元人民币）的 C 轮融资。根据路透社的报道，该企业估值达到 70 亿美元（现汇率约合 468.01 亿元人民币）。英国政府主权人工智能风险投资基金和英国商业银行在本轮融资中向 Fractile 提供了支持，其它投资者包括谷歌风投部门、贝莱德等。Fractile 目标是构建出真正意义上更快的 AI 推理计算硬件，无需在吞吐、模型尺寸、上下文长度上进行权衡。此外有消息称，Anthropic 有意于 2027 年部署 Fractile 的“模拟内存计算”芯片。英国人工智能大臣 Kanishka Narayan 表示：长期以来，英国虽然孕育了世界上一些最杰出的科学理念，但这些理念所创造的技术、产业和财富却大多在其他地方得以实现。我们决心改变这一现状。如果要让人工智能真正服务于英国人民、加强我们的公共服务并在全国范围内创造优质就业岗位，英国就必须自主研发更多支撑人工智能发展的核心技术。Fractile 体现了英国最卓越的雄心，它汇聚了世界一流的芯片设计、工程和人工智能专业知识，致力于开发更快、更便宜且更节能的硬件。通过支持 Fractile 这样的杰出英国企业，我们确保英国拥有塑造人工智能未来的工业实力和自主能力，并将由此产生的就业机会和经济收益带回全国各地的社区。相关阅读：《消息称 Anthropic 与 Fractile 达成初步供应合同，后者寻求 65 亿美元估值》

articles.title: 豆包工作接入 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash、Kimi K3.1 Pro 等第三方模型，同步上线额度消耗倍率与限时优惠
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，豆包官方今日宣布，豆包工作完成了一次产品更新，拓展更多可调用的模型，并同步引入了一套按实际消耗计价的额度调节机制。此前，豆包工作在模型侧仅提供豆包 2.1 Lite 与豆包 2.1 Pro 两款自研模型。此次更新后，Kimi K3.1 Pro、GLM 5.3、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 作为首批第三方模型进入可选列表，用户可以在自研模型与第三方模型之间按任务需要自行切换。在此之前，10 月 29 日，豆包工作先向团队订阅版与企业订阅版客户开放了三方模型配置，企业无需另行向模型厂商采购或额外申请，用量直接扣除已有的 AI 点数。11 月 12 日的更新将这一能力扩展至更广泛的用户范围，并配套上线了面向所有用户的限时优惠计划。引入多模型后，成本差异成为不可回避的问题。不同模型在完成同一任务时的资源开销并不相同，豆包工作的做法是在模型选择页面直接标注每款模型的额度消耗倍率，倍率系数越低，完成同一任务消耗的额度越少。IT之家注：额度消耗倍率可以理解为不同模型完成同一任务时的“计价系数”，它不改变任务本身的复杂度，但决定了用户账户中的可用额度能以多快的速度被消耗，从而让用户在效果、速度与成本之间做出可见的权衡。这一设计的意义在于，用户不必再凭直觉猜测哪款模型“更划算”，选择依据被前置到了操作界面。限时优惠在两个层面展开。一是工作日及节假日的指定优惠时段内，使用参与活动的模型可享受额度消耗折扣。二是针对豆包 2.1 Lite 和 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 直接下调额度消耗倍率，两款模型本身定位偏向高频轻量任务，倍率下调后同等任务消耗更少，额度更耐用。另外，豆包工作简单小额任务仍保持免费。官方图显示，模型选择列表首项为“自动（小额免费）”，系统会根据任务规模自动匹配模型；当任务复杂度上升时，用户可手动切换至豆包 2.1 Pro 或第三方模型，按对应倍率计费。相关阅读：《豆包工作向企业客户推出第三方模型服务：含 Kimi 3.1 Pro、GLM 5.3、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 等》

articles.title: 遏制烦人的网页 Cookie 弹窗，苹果 Safari 27.3 浏览器拟引入新隐私选项
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，科技媒体 9to5Mac 昨日（11 月 11 日）发布博文，报道称在 iOS 27.3 首个 Beta 开发者预览版中，苹果公司计划为 Safari 浏览器引入“全局隐私控制”（Global Privacy Control，简称 GPC）选项，未来有望减少用户反复处理 Cookie 同意弹窗的麻烦。IT之家援引博文介绍，该选项位于“设置 → 应用 → Safari 浏览器 → 高级”中。按照苹果的说明，开启后，Safari 可以要求网站不要出售或共享用户数据。不过，苹果同时提醒，这可能导致部分网站无法正常运行，甚至完全无法使用。新闻记者 Nick Heer 指出，这项新标准实际上是替代“请勿追踪”（Do Not Track）功能，并具有全局效力，支持用户一次性表明其追踪偏好，理论上，之后就不会再看到 Cookie 同意横幅了。不过 9to5Mac 指出 Safari 浏览器启用该选项后，并不意味着能一键清除所有 Cookie 弹窗，实际效果仍取决于网站是否支持 GPC，以及当地法规是否要求网站遵守相关信号。报道称目前已有部分网站接入，但多数网站尚未支持。相关阅读：《苹果 iOS 27.3 开发者预览版 Beta 又一重要更新，Safari 浏览器支持自适应深色模式》《苹果 Safari 27.3 测试版浏览器上线：适配 iPhone Duo，引入垂直标签、Siri 帮你管网页》

articles.title: 长城首款 V8 混动超跑官宣：明年上市，魏建军称其对标法拉利 SF90
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，长城汽车董事长魏建军正式公布了长城首台超跑。魏建军表示，这款超级跑车的对标目标是法拉利，同时放出了新车与法拉利 SF90 的对比测试视频。据魏建军介绍，新车预计于 2026 年年底正式亮相，2027 年上市。魏建军表示，该车搭载的是国内首款自主研发的 4.0L 双涡轮增压 V8 发动机，并与 PHEV 插混系统结合。这台 V8 发动机的技术细节在 2026 年北京车展期间已部分公开。长城为超跑与 GT3 赛车同步开发的 GF 高性能架构中，4.0T V8 采用 90 度 V 角与 HOT V 型双涡轮布局，配备了赛道级电控软件和干式润滑系统。与之匹配的是全碳纤维单体壳座舱，重量低于 130kg，扭转刚度标称为 4 万 Nm / 度。长城此前公布的架构目标显示，民用超跑的系统功率将突破 1200 马力，推重比超过 0.68ps / kg。IT之家注：推重比指发动机功率与车辆重量的比值，在重量相近的前提下，推重比越高，加速和操控响应通常越直接。这套动力布局与法拉利 SF90、迈凯伦 Artura 等欧洲混动超跑属于同一技术品类：以中置 V8 提供持续的高功率输出，以电机改善低速响应和能耗。法拉利 SF90 的综合输出标称约 1000 马力，0-100km/h 加速在 2.5 秒级别。魏建军在微博中将这款车描述为“中国真正意义上的超跑”，并称“希望超越法拉利”。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 12 日消息，IDC 最新数据显示，2026 年第三季度中国平板电脑市场出货量为 660 万台，同比下降 22.3%，成本压力加速向需求端传导，市场调整幅度进一步扩大。IDC 表示，Q3 消费市场受涨价影响持续收缩，商用市场则在需求前置后逐步回归常态，厂商竞争及市场需求结构也随之发生变化。IDC 指出，伴随成本上涨压力充分向销售端传导，市场出货量降幅较上半年显著扩大，单季度出货量在连续 12 个季度后首次低于 700 万台，降幅也创下 2020 年第一季度新冠疫情以来的最大值，市场首次迎来同比双位数下滑。从市场表现来看，第三季度有三个值得关注的变化：一是消费与商用市场的表现背离仍在延续，但商用市场增长恐难持续；二是头部厂商格局相对稳定，中游厂商份额继续提升；三是成本上涨推动市场需求加速分化，入门级市场收缩与中高价位段升级同步发生。消费市场涨价导致销量折损，商用市场库存补充进入尾声2026 年第三季度，中国消费与商用平板市场出货量继续呈现背离趋势。消费平板出货量同比下降 24.9%，伴随头部厂商接连上调产品售价，市场均价环比提升 8.6%，价格上涨对消费者购买意愿的抑制进一步显现。商用平板市场出货量同比增长 9.6%。作为教育行业需求高峰期，7、8 月厂商继续加码教育市场布局，但 9 月需求已明显减弱。与此同时，华为、荣耀自 7 月起上调商用平板售价，也对后续市场需求带来压力。随着前期需求前置及渠道库存补充逐步进入尾声，商用市场增长势头预计难以延续。竞争格局稳中有变，厂商持续调整产品布局以缓和涨价压力、寻求增长轨道2026 年第三季度，中国平板市场前五厂商排名与上一季度保持一致，但中游集团市场份额继续提升。成本上涨背景下，厂商在产品结构、渠道布局及价格调整节奏上的差异进一步显现。华为继续位列市场第一。尽管其消费及商用平板均迎来较大幅度的价格上调，但凭借鸿蒙生态互联能力、品牌影响力及完善的渠道布局，华为仍保持市场领导地位。与此同时，华为平板产品迭代持续推进，接续产品配置较上一代明显升级，带动产品结构优化。Apple 位列市场第二。6 月底 Apple 上调其平板产品售价，导致第三季度出货量同比下降 27.2%。价格上涨削弱 Apple 平板的竞争力，市场规模承压的同时，其产品结构也明显向低价数字版机型倾斜。联想位列市场第三，出货量同比增长 33.2%，是前五厂商中唯一实现增长的厂商。消费市场方面，小新系列保持性价比优势的同时拯救者系列快速发展，第三季度出货量占比接近半数；商用市场出货节奏相对稳定，价格优势逐步回归，市场份额升至第一。小米位列市场第四。伴随平板 9 系列新品上市，小米市场份额企稳回升。其中，小米平板 9 Pro Max 凭借自研芯片玄戒 O3 首发优势获得较好的市场反馈，提升品牌声量的同时，也推动了小米平板价位段向上拓展。荣耀延续市场第五位。消费市场受成本上涨冲击持续收缩，季度新品平板 X10 Pro Max 凭借价格优势及教育场景拓展，帮助荣耀拓展 13 英寸及以上大屏市场布局；商用市场则在教育采购高峰期下延续高速增长，并通过配置调整优化产品价格。市场需求加速分化，入门级市场收缩，中高价位段需求上移受成本上涨影响，平板产品价格逐步抬升，部分厂商被迫放弃入门级价位区间，千元以下入门级市场规模同比缩减 51.4%。与此同时，中高价位段份额持续提升。2026 年第三季度，中国平板市场 3000 元及以上机型出货量占比约为 45%，环比提升近 10 个百分点。当前背景下，中高价位段需求拓展主要来自两类场景：一是结合大尺寸屏幕及 PC 级生态迁移的轻办公与学习场景，二是以小尺寸产品为代表的电竞及随行场景。伴随价格持续上涨或盘踞高位，厂商迫切需要通过性能、生态及场景体验提升平板的产品价值，为中高端产品创造更充分的溢价空间。展望未来2026 年第三季度，中国平板市场出货量迎来双位数下滑，成本上涨对市场的影响进一步放大。消费市场需求明显收缩，商用市场也逐步进入前期需求释放后的调整阶段，整体市场面临较大压力。IDC 预计，此轮成本压力将持续至 2028 年，2026 年第四季度及 2027 年中国平板市场出货量规模将面临较大挑战。价格上涨导致消费者换机决策更加谨慎，厂商也需要重新评估产品迭代节奏、市场备货及销售目标，以平稳驶过不确定性较强的市场阶段。与此同时，市场也将在本轮调整中进一步推动平板产品的场景化布局，围绕核心用户群体挖掘细分需求，加快 AI 能力与实际应用场景的融合，持续提升平板产品的价值定位，为后续市场复苏与增长拓展新的空间。

articles.content:
I’ve had acne for 10 years and I'm so exhausted of dont know what happened. 
So, I'm building AcneAlly to learn you overtime to figure out what's causing your acne, and to give personalized support. 
Instead of  tracking your skin or logging daily habits, you can just talk or interact with it like a companion. You can share about your acne, share your concerns, or ask anything you want. Based on what you share, it uses Al to reasoning to make guesses about what could be causing your acne. As you share more, it update it understanding abt you, its guesses abt the cause and it suggestions.
This is an early version, and there's still a lot to improve.
I'd love to hear your feedback!
Thanks for checking it out!

articles.content:

Abstract: Closed-loop autonomous experimentation can accelerate scientific discovery, but implementation effort limits accessibility. Across three experiments, 61-67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, while the share of methodological and scientific contributions increased from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56-61% in later experiments. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12934v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. We introduce EarthRecord, a benchmark built on the raw record of 56 sites: four decades of Landsat, MODIS, VIIRS, and Sentinel-2 data, with cloud masking and cross-sensor harmonization left to the agent. It poses 238 land-change questions across ten analysis tasks, scored against withheld references from global products, agreement among methods, and visual interpretation. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12935v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Topic monitoring is the task of labelling the topic of each token in a model's response during generation. Activation-based monitors that run at generation time have so far been trained to detect harmful content and are limited to two or three classes. We introduce TopicScope, a framework for training causal topic classifiers on SAE features that assign a topic to every token, so that the label can change partway through a response. We train three detector architectures on synthetic multi-topic conversations covering seven topics. Across Gemma-3 1B and 4B, monitors trained on features extracted from prefill hidden states were able to generalise to decoding. We also found that the classifiers are robust to perturbations, losing at most 5 macro-F1 points when off-topic asides are inserted, topics are removed or sections are reordered. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12936v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Intelligent landslide detection is essential for disaster prevention. However, existing models primarily focus on isolated visual tasks, require extensive labeled data, and lack deep analytical and scene-understanding capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose LandslideFM, the first unified foundation model that connects visual perception tasks with contextual interpretation of landslides. Specifically, LandslideFM adapts to multiple visual tasks via a Source-Agreement Graduated Trust semi-supervised learning framework that leverages limited labeled data alongside abundant unlabeled data. Furthermore, predicted landslide regions provide explicit spatial guidance to a Vision-Language Model adapted through parameter-efficient fine-tuning, enabling comprehensive landslide reasoning. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12937v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Do large language models represent psychological constructs internally, or do they only generate outputs that resemble psychometric structure? We address this question using a cross-persona paradigm across 14 model variants from two families (Llama 3 and Qwen 2.5, 0.5B-14B, base and instruct). Given responses on one psychological scale from real individuals (N = 272 Taiwanese university students), models predict responses on six other scales. At the behavioral level, larger variants reproduce and amplify human cross-scale correlations; amplification persists after correcting the seven-scale human correlations for measurement attenuation. articles.title: Graph Visualizations in Prompts for Knowledge Graph Question Answering
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12938v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study when and how multimodal input improves knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) in large vision--language models. Using a controlled evaluation over 1,500 WebQSP and CWQ questions and six VLMs within a fixed KGQA pipeline, we compare text-only prompting against text-plus-graph visualization at the per-question level and analyze performance changes as a function of reasoning complexity, model size, and image layout. Adding a graph image yields an average gain of 1.85 F1 points, driven by strong precision improvements on low-complexity questions (+4.65 F1). Mixed-effects and regression analyses show that these multimodal gains do not depend strongly on model scale, but are highly sensitive to graph layout: image-only settings sharply degrade performance, hierarchical Graphviz layouts outperform less organized renderings, and decomposing large subgraphs into separated paths yields the largest improvements. articles.title: AI Governance Should Prioritize Control and Knowledge Boundaries Over Limiting Intelligence
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12941v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The rapid proliferation of autonomously acting AI agents makes the governance of agentic systems urgent. We propose the competence circuit, summarized as IKC + KC + C, that decomposes an agent's real-world impact into three pathways: intelligence-mediated discovery, procedural know-how, and direct control. Using the canonical fast-takeoff debate as a stress test, we formalize the conditions for intelligence-mediated fast takeoff as a conjunction jointly sufficient for fast catastrophic supremacy, showing that most rely on rapid knowledge acquisition or control attainment rather than intelligence alone. We operationalize epistemic intelligence as hypothesis-selection efficiency and validate this framework via stochastic simulation on NK fitness landscapes across six scenarios spanning the conjunctive chain. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12942v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) predict from a labelled context in a single forward pass. A recent benchmark reported that they decisively outperform tree ensembles for customer churn, but it compared them with untuned gradient-boosted trees (GBDTs) and scored only ranking metrics, while a retention campaign is judged in money. We re-evaluate TabPFN-2.5, TabPFN-3.5, TabPFN-3.5-Fast and TabICL v2 against Optuna-tuned GBDTs on five public telecom churn datasets over 10 seeded splits. We separate three questions: whether a model ranks churners well, whether that ranking earns more expected maximum profit (EMP), and whether its probabilities can drive a threshold policy. With a split-aware test and Holm correction over 20 pre-declared comparisons, TabPFN-3.5 earns significantly more EMP than the best tuned GBDT on Cell2Cell (1.9%) and Iranian (7.6%), and these two gains also hold against each of the three tuned GBDTs separately. articles.title: SetPrint: Black-Box LLM Fingerprinting via Setwise Correspondence of Response Changes
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12950v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Black-box LLM fingerprinting aims to determine whether a target model was derived from a source model when only the output responses to input queries are observable. One way to reveal this relationship is to perturb each query and observe the resulting responses of both models, yielding two corresponding sets of response variations. These sets provide two complementary sources of information: the relations among response changes within each set, and the correspondence of response changes between the two sets. Existing approaches, however, have not fully exploited both. We introduce \textbf{SetPrint}, a training-free method that jointly captures both within-set relations and between-set correspondence. SetPrint expresses each response change relative to the mean change of its own set, and then compares changes from the two models that were induced by the same perturbation. Abstract: Enterprises increasingly use large language model agents to execute standard operating procedures (SOPs): long, branching, tool-intensive workflows. Yet there is little controlled evidence for choosing among competing agentic architectures. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12954v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled weight-space programming (WSP), which directly generates neural network weights without gradient-based optimization. However, extending WSP to physical problems remains challenging, particularly in achieving both solution accuracy and physical consistency. In this paper, we propose Physics2Weight (PtW), a framework that extends WSP to solving partial differential equations by directly generating neural network weights and editing architectures based on governing equations and initial and boundary conditions. PtW introduces physics-constrained prompting and physics-guided architecture editing, combined with iterative weight refinement from WSP, to improve solution accuracy and physical consistency without gradient-based optimization. articles.content:

Abstract: Recent advances in large models have accelerated AI for Science toward agentic science, where AI agents autonomously conduct scientific discovery. Realising this vision requires closing the loop between computational reasoning and physical experimentation, positioning self-driving laboratories (SDLs) as critical enablers. However, existing SDLs exhibit a fundamental paradox: foundation model integration has increased linguistic sophistication while severing physical grounding. By treating models as disembodied planners that output symbolic workflows for separate robotic systems, current architectures inherently block the development of embodied experimental intuition. articles.content:

Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate SQL and SQL--Python workflows for investment research, but ensuring point-in-time (PIT) validity remains challenging. Agents must enforce disclosure cutoffs and select the appropriate historical states and record versions throughout data retrieval and financial analysis. We evaluate nine agent configurations on all tasks, with result accuracy ranging from 16.2\% to 36.8\%. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12970v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) show strong potential for social media content moderation, but their trustworthiness beyond overall accuracy remains underexplored. We introduce TrustMod-SM, a benchmark of roughly 29,000 instances across eight datasets, to evaluate LLM moderators on five dimensions: trustfulness, fairness, safety, robustness, and context integrity. Evaluating 16 open-weight models (0.5B-284B parameters, spanning text-only and vision-language architectures) and one closed frontier model, we find persistent trustworthiness gaps. Higher detection accuracy often coincides with greater demographic disparity, and models frequently comply with concealment or exaggeration prompts, assign high confidence to wrong predictions, rarely escalate ambiguous cases, and struggle to separate hate speech from counter-speech or reclaimed language (especially below 8B parameters). articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12992v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Energy-based models (EBMs) assign a scalar energy to every joint value of the observed and predicted variables. In decision models, the prediction is chosen from a finite list of options provided with each input. Inference then reduces to comparing the energies of the options, and training lowers the energy of the correct option relative to the others. A complete decision must also account for the possibility that no option is acceptable. However, the energies learned by a standard EBM define only relative compatibility: adding the same input-dependent quantity to all energies leaves the predictions, the Gibbs distribution, and the usual training losses unchanged. The model therefore has no learned reference level against which to decide whether any option fits. Abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) often report a finding because the question names it; standard benchmarks miss this. From public segmentation datasets we build counterfactual views without manual annotation: the lesion erased by inpainting, a same-shape control edit elsewhere, and unedited lesion-free images. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12955v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Time-series classifiers deployed in risk-sensitive domains must be (1) accurate, (2) interpretable, and (3) able to abstain when evidence is weak. Existing methods do not deliver all 3 at once, and the obstacle is structural, rather than logistical. Meaningful temporal patterns cannot be defined without knowing segment boundaries, yet meaningful boundaries cannot be placed without knowing which patterns to expect. Existing approaches break this circularity by using fixed windows or expert-annotated vocabularies, thereby sacrificing at least one of the 3 properties. We introduce ConceptTime, which closes the loop through a single self-supervised signal. A frozen probabilistic forecaster predicts a distribution over the next observation at every timestep of the sequence. Abstract: DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) reduces the computational cost of attention through token-level selection. However, its indexer still scores the entire causal prefix for each query, making indexing a dominant source of latency in long-context inference. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12964v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While federated reinforcement learning (RL) has traditionally guaranteed high efficiency in homogeneous environments, collaboration is often hindered when agents possess distinct goals. In this paper, we flip this paradigm, framing reward heterogeneity not as a hurdle to consensus, but as a structural asset that catalyzes exploration. We first propose Personalized Federated Upper Confidence Bound Value Iteration (PF-UCBVI), which achieves optimal linear speedup by decoupling shared dynamics from personalized objectives. To eliminate the risks of explicit exploration, we then introduce Personalized Federated Exploration-Free Value Iteration (PF-EFVI), a purely greedy algorithm that leverages reward diversity to ensure state-action coverage. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12974v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Time-series forecasting has recently seen a paradigm shift with the introduction of foundation-style models that adapt large pretrained language architectures to sequential data. However, effectively exposing fundamental temporal structures, such as trend, scale, and temporal dependence, to these models remains an open challenge, particularly when the available observations are limited. In this paper, we conduct an exploratory empirical study across different generations of forecasting architectures and propose StatPrompt-LLM, a lightweight statistical refinement of Time-LLM. StatPrompt-LLM augments the existing Time-LLM prompting mechanism with dataset-level statistical information and introduces a zero-initialised autoregressive bypass as a complementary linear forecasting pathway. articles.title: MADSNet: A Multi-Scale Axial-Attentive Dense Spiking Network for Spike Camera Image Reconstruction
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12980v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spike cameras encode dynamic scenes into high-temporal-resolution binary spike streams for efficient high-speed vision. Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) can process such signals with sparse and accumulate-only computation, existing SNN-based reconstruction methods are typically shallow and still lag behind ANN-based models in reconstruction fidelity. This paper proposes MADSNet, a Multi-scale Axial-attentive Dense Spiking Network for spike camera image reconstruction. MADSNet adopts a hierarchical spiking encoder--decoder, where a multi-scale spike stem extracts early features, axial spike attention captures long-range dependencies, a dense spiking bottleneck enhances feature reuse, and a spike-to-continuous decoder reconstructs continuous intensity images from spike-domain representations. Experiments on gray-scale and color spike reconstruction show that MADSNet outperforms SSIR by 4.3 dB PSNR and Spk2ImgNet by 1.94 dB on SREDS.

articles.content:

Abstract: Does a useful self-update remain useful after the model updates again? Third Eye separates immediate performance from the outcome of a further native update. We evaluate five 3-8B backbones on math and code: 64 fresh runs, three candidates per run, and three continuations per candidate. Selection and final scoring use disjoint items. In the balanced Qwen3-4B/Llama-3.2-3B comparison, immediate-selected utility is near zero, but continuation reduces it by 1.78 percentage points (simultaneous 95% interval [0.68, 2.88]). Candidate-averaged immediate utility is already negative: selection partly accounts for the apparently neutral first step. Continuation also lowers utility for SmolLM3-3B and Llama-3.1-8B; Qwen3-8B remains inconclusive. Target and out-of-distribution losses dominate retention changes. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12998v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Linear probes are a standard method to study geometric structures, such as helices and circles, from the activations of large language models (LLMs), and such structure is often taken as evidence that the model computes with it. Probe accuracy alone cannot establish this, because it conflates four separate claims. These are (1) that the concept is decodable from the activations, (2) that they form a specific shape, (3) that the shape belongs to the probed concept rather than to a related concept the model also represents, and (4) that the output of the model depends on the shape. We call these claims decodability, shape, ownership, and causal use, and we test them separately with a four-stage Bayesian pipeline. Abstract: Generation, imputation, and prediction query different aspects of the same tabular distribution, but are usually evaluated separately. articles.title: Branch-and-Commit for Frozen RL Agents: When and Where to Spend Test-Time Compute
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13003v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning agents are often deployed with policies that cannot be retrained or modified. In digital environments whose states can be copied and resumed, an operator has another option: sample several continuations from the current state, evaluate them, and continue from the endpoint of the selected branch. We call this procedure branch-and-commit. We study when it improves return, what produces the improvement, and where its computational budget should be spent. Across four environments, two frozen policies, five continuation verifiers, and a model-free selection rule, we find that the benefit of branching depends on dispersion: the difference between the best candidate return and the mean candidate return. Branching provides no benefit in low-dispersion settings, while increasing return by 12.8% in our main Craftax-Medium setting. articles.title: The Shape of a Program: Path Signatures for Trace-to-Program Induction
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13005v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Synthesizing programs from execution traces is a fundamental challenge in algorithmic interpretability and the reverse engineering of complex systems. We bring a rough-path-theoretic perspective to program induction, treating execution traces as high-dimensional rough paths and encoding them with the path signature transform, a tool from stochastic analysis whose expectation provably characterizes the distribution of traces a program induces. On three program-induction domains, Karel, List, and RASP, our log-signature trace encoder outperforms LSTM, Transformer, and Fourier baselines in almost every setting, with its largest margins when training data is scarce. We further observe that the trace-to-program pipeline is naturally contractive: it often produces valid programs that are shorter than the ground truth. We turn this into a bootstrapping procedure that exposes redundancy in the ground-truth supervision without any external oracle

articles.content:

Abstract: Synthetic data augmentation promises to scale offline reinforcement learning beyond fixed logged datasets, but leading diffusion-based generators model the transition tuple (state, action, next state, reward, terminal) as a monolith: no single factor can be natively redrawn in isolation. Across twelve D4RL locomotion and maze benchmarks, TD3+BC and IQL agents trained on FaST transitions match the SynthER diffusion baseline while generating transitions over 90x faster. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13057v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Indoor localization commonly combines WiFi received signal strength indicator (RSSI) fingerprints with inertial measurements. However, these sensor streams are sampled asynchronously at different rates; therefore, observations rarely align in time and may be missing or stale. Most existing methods resample the data onto a shared clock and process each modality using a separate branch. We instead present a continuous-time transformer that represents observations as an unordered set of timestamped tokens. Each token encodes its measurement, modality, and elapsed time since acquisition. Abstract: Banks now train foundation models on ordered sequences of customer events such as transactions, app sessions, and authorizations. Abstract: Brain networks exhibit modular organization, where community structures vary substantially across individuals and diseases. Understanding these individual differences is crucial for advancing both basic neuroscience research and precision medicine. However, widely used predefined group-level brain atlases often overlook this heterogeneity. Abstract: Time series from real-world systems are often accompanied by text, such as a report on an event that affects them. Two common tasks on these series are understanding, e.g., answering questions about a series, and forecasting its future values. Both tasks require reasoning over the series and the text together. articles.title: SELD: Detecting Silent Evidence Loss in Context Compression beyond the Answer
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12903v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Context compression is now routine for language models with long inputs, but a compressed context is useful only if it keeps the evidence for the answer. Existing checks compare the reader model's answer or its most likely words, and thus miss a frequent failure, silent evidence loss: key evidence is removed while the answer stays the same, leaving the answer unsupported and risky for other models that reuse the context. To address this challenge, we propose SELD (Silent Evidence Loss Detector), which needs no training and no labels. Its principle is that when evidence is lost, a reader model's preferences among the answers it leaves unsaid shift even if its answer does not, so comparing these preferences before and after compression reveals losses that answer checks cannot see. Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being deployed in clinical documentation workflows, where clinicians review and edit their outputs before use. Abstract: This work presents a new benchmark that aims to address the limitations of current methods for evaluating LLMs in Brazilian Portuguese. The results show that model size, by itself, does not determine performance; several medium-sized models outperformed larger models in the protocols evaluated. Specific models for Portuguese, in general, did not perform above average, despite their targeted training. Abstract: Offline web-behavior benchmarks frequently insert the demonstrated action into a finite candidate set and then measure reranking. We show that this protocol can create a candidate-support confound: when the target is outside training support while all distractors are sampled from that support, support membership identifies the gold action without modeling behavior. articles.title: Capacity Allocation at the Source: Sparse Target Optimization for LLM Knowledge Editing
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12995v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Knowledge editing has emerged as a promising approach for efficiently updating embedded knowledge in large language models (LLMs). It first computes an ideal target hidden state that steers the LLM toward the new output, and then edits the model parameters so that the original hidden state is mapped to this target. While most existing methods focus on the second stage of parameter editing in preserving other knowledge, we find that the upstream construction of the target hidden state also plays an important role in allocating the model's limited capacity space. We first establish a theoretical connection between interference in the parameter space and interference between target hidden states, showing that the two are positively correlated. Building on this insight, we propose a simple yet effective $\ell_1$ regularization method that prunes away unnecessary ``tentacles'' of each knowledge vector, retaining only the essential components.

articles.title: khammoon: From a Linguistic Guideline to a Thai Morpheme Segmenter
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13012v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Thai is written without spaces between words, making segmentation a foundational step in most Thai NLP pipelines. Existing tools primarily reproduce the word-level conventions of corpora such as BEST; however, because the notion of a "word" in Thai lacks a unified linguistic consensus, these conventions struggle with productive compounding, leading to arbitrary boundaries and ambiguity in downstream representations. Instead, we propose operating at the morphological level, focusing on khammoon, the smallest atomic unit that carries meaning. Segmenting at the morphemic level provides an explicit, consistent morphological representation that eliminates compounding ambiguity. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13107v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly trusted with mathematical, scientific and engineering work, yet their mistakes are often confidently written and hard to spot. A single wrong step tends to propagate, making the model waste inference tokens following a false premise. Existing safeguards either check only the final answer and restart from scratch, or rely on a verifier LLM that competes for GPU capacity and slows down response time. We propose online, deterministic verification: many kinds of reasoning steps can be validated by code, so a step can be verified in real time, as it is written, without any model call or GPU use. Whenever a check fails, we point out the mistake and let the model continue from the same spot. We demonstrate this approach on symbolic mathematics, where derivations already contain explicit expressions that a computer algebra system can check in milliseconds. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13207v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cultural adaptation in dialogue systems refers to the ability to generate responses that conform to linguistic norms and social expectations across different cultures. However, existing dialogue generation approaches pay limited attention to the role of personality in shaping cultural expression and communication style. We therefore propose HiCAP, a novel framework that integrates personality traits into culturally adaptive dialogue generation. HiCAP employs a personality-conditioned control mechanism that hierarchically modulates response style by first aligning it with the cultural tone and then refining linguistic expression and content according to individual personality attributes. To embed these factors, the model combines supervised fine-tuning and instruction-based tuning, supported by dynamic instruction templates and multi-agent demonstrations to capture diverse combinations of culture and personality. Abstract: Reasoning models write a reasoning trace at every turn of a multi-turn tool session, and later turns read this history. Across 94k ShareGPT conversations, 73 percent of user interactions span multiple turns. Upstream providers bind each trace to its issuer, so a request forwarded across issuers arrives with its history deleted, and the task cost of this stripping remains unmeasured. To the best of our knowledge, this paper presents the first direct, blind, multi-seed measurement of full reasoning-history deletion in multi-turn tool calling, through three rendering conditions, seven open-weight reasoning models, three seeds, 794 tasks, and the official checker. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13339v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In social science research, text annotation is a fundamental task that is traditionally a costly, hard-to-scale manual process. Researchers have used large language models (LLMs) to perform annotation by writing a definition of a concept into a prompt - a rule that determines whether a label should be attributed to a text depending on its content. However, concepts such as hate speech, fake news, and terrorism typically have several theoretically defensible competing definitions. It is also unknown whether the model actually applied the definition to provide the label or the label was based on the model's pretrained notion of the concept. articles.title: Understanding Students' Rationales for AI-Mediated Cheating: An Instructor Perspective from Online Forums Analysis
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13358v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The extensive adoption of AI has precipitated a crisis in academic integrity. While studies attempt to quantify cheating, less is known about the motivations instructors believe students have for using AI in prohibited ways. We analyze 2.01 million posts on r/Professors to understand how instructors perceive students' justifications for AI-mediated cheating. Our qualitative analyses reveal four primary themes: (1) Academic System Gaming, (2) Digital-Academic Literacy Gap, (3) Performance Anxiety, and (4) Normalization of Dishonesty.

Abstract: In teaching and learning environments, cheating and the violation of academic integrity have always been one of the challenges, involving different levels of concerns such as administrative, personal knowledge, learning, and equity. Abstract: Distilling flow matching models for one-step generation generally follows two paradigms. Trajectory alignment supervises the student with the teacher's probability flow ODE, but its performance degrades under very small sampling budgets. Distribution matching directly optimizes the generated distribution, but estimating its reverse Kullback-Leibler gradient typically requires a separate network to track the evolving student score. We propose trajectory-regularized distribution distillation (TRD), which combines distribution-level and trajectory-level supervision through a momentum-mixture policy predicted in a single student forward pass. Abstract: Multimodal (e.g. vision-language, in this work) attribution aims to interpret the models without access to ground-truth explanatory supervision. Abstract: Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. Abstract: Complete-or-reject reporting of surgical action triplets can discard a correctly identified instrument and action when the target is uncertain. Each selected instance retains its predicted mask and labels while hierarchical correctness scores guide instrument (I), instrument-verb (IV), or complete instrument-verb-target (IVT) reporting. Abstract: Ancient books preserve invaluable cultural heritage, yet their images often suffer from complex degradations caused by long-term ageing, environmental exposure, and physical damage. Abstract: Recent work on latent-free diffusion transformers has demonstrated the feasibility of training image generators without a latent VAE. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12949v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Maze navigation requires localization from sparse, repetitive geometry, planning through narrow corridors, and control that stays safe when the estimate or the map is wrong. We present Maze Runner, an open autonomy stack in C++ and ROS 2 that addresses these needs end to end on a simulated Husarion ROSbot XL with a 2D LiDAR in Gazebo. Perception extracts wall lines from each scan with RANSAC and total least squares, with per-line uncertainty. The same line front end feeds two estimators: an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) that localizes against a line map built from the maze mesh, and an EKF SLAM variant that builds the line map online. Planning runs online on an inflated occupancy grid with A* plus line-of-sight shortcutting, or with a forward-only Hybrid A*. Abstract: Robot agents can improve reusable skills, planning procedures, and recovery strategies from execution feedback, yet a fixed practice source leaves the search for new weaknesses unchanged. Abstract: Reliable medical laboratory automation requires robots to complete entire workflows in protocol order while handling changes during execution. A robot may execute each motion correctly yet fail the workflow by confusing visually similar stages or stalling after human intervention. We present Robo-MLT, a dual-system framework that couples explicit workflow monitoring with learned action generation. A vision--language planner composes an ordered atomic-skill sequence from the protocol and the initial workspace observation. A multiframe execution monitor detects when the active skill has completed or become infeasible, then advances the workflow or triggers replanning. A skill-conditioned vision--language--action policy generates the manipulation trajectories, and an asynchronous runtime coordinates it with the monitor. Abstract: We introduce Latent Barrier Steering (LBS), a hierarchical semantic-to-path framework for safe flow-matching-based generative planning. Existing control-barrier-function (CBF) safety filters for diffusion and flow-matching planners act locally on generated samples, either during sampling or after prediction. Such repair is effective for small violations, but can struggle when a new constraint blocks the whole selected behavior mode rather than merely perturbing it locally. LBS decouples behavior selection from path certification through two coordinated interventions: it first steers the generator's behavior latent toward rollouts with larger safety margin, then decodes the steered latent and applies a path-space CBF quadratic program (QP) only for residual violations. Abstract: In cooperative object manipulation, the placement of pushing contacts determines whether force closure can be achieved and agents can generate arbitrary forces and torques on the object correspondingly. Abstract: Planning planetary rover trajectories under probabilistic uncertainty is a multi-objective optimization problem that science teams currently iteratively solve and verify by hand. This process becomes impractical when timelines and constraints frequently shift throughout the mission planning phase. articles.title: Rhythmic-Semantic Co-Speech Gestures for Emotional Dialogue in Robots
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13472v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Co-speech gestures can increase engagement and improve speech understanding. Yet, most data-driven robot systems generate either rhythmic beat-like motion or semantically meaningful iconic gestures, but not both. We present an emotion-aware rhythmic-semantic co-speech gesture system that generates iconic and beat behaviors in real time from text and the robot's internal emotional state. We formalize the task of beat-iconic gesture generation using emotion and propose lightweight models that predict iconic timing and intensity, then fill the remaining spans with emotion-conditioned beats at an appropriate intensity level. We train on the BEAT2 dataset and deploy the system on the social robot Haru. In an online user study with 60 participants, our method shows stronger speech-gesture alignment and is preferred over baseline methods.

articles.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
articles.content: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. It also remains unclear how much of a foundation model must be adapted, and what determines this. We adapted a foundation model, DINOv2, with strategies ranging from tuning only its bias terms to full fine-tuning, and compared it with U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch. Experiments covered colonoscopy, breast ultrasound and dermoscopy, with testing on held-out data from the training source and on independent datasets from other institutions. The adapted foundation model generalised better on every external dataset. Within the training distribution, the task-specific models remained competitive when training data were abundant, and delineated boundaries more precisely, while the foundation model more often missed small lesions. Only a small fraction of the foundation model required adaptation, and the capacity needed was determined by the imaging domain rather than by the adaptation method. A widely used polyp test set was also found to duplicate images from another benchmark. Foundation-model adaptation is therefore warranted where models must work across sites, with capacity selected on the target domain.

articles.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
articles.content: DeepLearning (DL)-based Computer-Aided Diagnostic (CAD) systems have shown great promise in supporting clinicians, but their performance heavily depends on the availability of large, well-annotated datasets. In medical lesion detection, the scarcity of comprehensive, stan dardized annotations and the heterogeneity of existing datasets limit the development of robust foundation models. In this work, we introduce a novel approach to building a multi-domain foundation model for le sion detection by integrating diverse medical image datasets annotated for both anatomical structures and abnormalities. We first propose a student-teacher training strategy to effectively combine datasets with heterogeneous label spaces, mitigating catastrophic forgetting, and im proving feature learning. In addition, building on our previously pro posed example-based EM-DETR framework, we adapt it to jointly learn from multiple domain-specific datasets, enabling fine-grained, example driven detection across modalities. Our model achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) results, with image-level AUC scores exceeding previous SOTA by 1% point on four key findings in CXRs. We achieve a leading mAP50 in CXRs and mammography, surpassing EM-DETR trained on a single dataset by 2-3% points. This approach paves the way for scalable foundation models in medical imaging that leverage heterogeneous data while maintaining robust and generalizable performance.

articles.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
articles.content: We present TorchCurves, a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives. Its central operation maps batches of scalar inputs to points on curves represented in B-spline or Legendre polynomial bases, with differentiation through both inputs and coefficients. Curve coefficients can be optimized jointly with the surrounding model or produced by another network. The library provides trainable modules, reusable basis modules, and a functional interface, supporting applications ranging from continuous feature embeddings to Kolmogorov-Arnold networks and functional regression. Its implementation combines classical evaluation algorithms with vectorized PyTorch operations, emphasizing readability and maintainability without custom hardware kernels. Timing experiments compare curve evaluation against NumPy and SciPy and KAN training against EfficientKAN across a range of problem sizes. The results illustrate where this generality remains computationally practical and where overhead is substantial. Library is available on GitHub at https://github.com/alexshtf/torchcurves.

articles.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
articles.content: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. We introduce AutoScaffold, a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student's training experience into adaptive scaffolds, with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. A frozen teacher periodically examines this experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs scaffolds in two forms: (i) strategies shared across a class of tasks and (ii) hints for individual hard tasks, adjusting the content and amount of support as the student learns. The scaffolds are removed at evaluation. We apply the same framework to ALFWorld, search-based QA, mathematical reasoning, and GPU kernel generation. When evaluated without scaffolds, students trained with AutoScaffold outperform those trained with the corresponding RL baselines in all four domains, with gains of 7.2 points in ALFWorld success and 4.0 points in average QA exact match. On GPU kernel generation, AutoScaffold increases the fraction of tasks with a correct kernel that runs faster than the PyTorch reference by up to 5.0 points. On math, our student surpasses QuestA's reported accuracy using approximately one-third as many student training steps. Analyses show that the teacher identifies a different failure in each task class and shifts its scaffolds from step-by-step workflows to targeted fixes as the student improves, and that its revised scaffolds help the student learn more than keeping the previous scaffold or using no scaffold.

articles.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
articles.content: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. To recover that alternative, we introduce Contrastive Discovery, which replaces the single hypothesis with a contrast set, a scientific question paired with mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive competing explanations. Each experiment is scored by how its evidence redistributes belief across the set, and the question is resolved when belief concentrates on one explanation. Because contrast sets change only the unit an agent proposes and scores, an existing agent can use them to re-evaluate evidence it has already collected or to guide its search. Across six domains, $89\%$ of the pointwise candidates with the largest belief shifts are rejections. On the same evidence, contrast sets resolve $73\%$ of these candidates to a specific alternative. When contrast sets guide search, the agent resolves $67\%$ more questions than pointwise surprisal under the same experiment budget. In a blinded study, $38$ human experts chose the same explanation on $78\%$ of resolved questions and on $82\%$ of questions where the pointwise agent rejected its hypothesis and stopped. Together, these results support explicit competing explanations as a way for discovery agents to resolve more scientific questions from the same evidence and validation budget.

articles.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
articles.content: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes. Expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores perform near chance, highlighting the difficulty of interpreting available chemical signals. To investigate automated ranking, we introduce PyriteRep, a structured representation of molecular geometry, protein-ligand interactions, and physicochemical scores, and develop two LLM-based agents: PyriteReasoner, which directly compares poses through text-based reasoning, and PyriteFeaturizer, which generates executable code to construct features for logistic regression, optionally incorporating features derived from LLM subcalls. These agents achieve up to 67% and 74% accuracy, respectively, exceeding observed expert performance. LLM-guided feature discovery generally outperforms direct reasoning, while Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) improves open-weight models, enabling them to match or surpass closed-source frontier models in our evaluations. These results establish Pyrite as a challenging test of pose-ranking ability and highlight LLM-guided feature discovery as a promising approach to interpret and combine the outputs of computational chemistry tools.

articles.title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
articles.content: Connectome-constrained models are often used to argue that a measured wiring diagram outperforms shuffled or rewired wiring, and hence that structure shapes function. Such comparisons can confound wiring with how the models are tuned: a connectome fixes who connects to whom, not the excitability, gains or plasticity rates the model also needs, and modellers often tune these until the real-wiring model works. We separate three estimands: physiology tuned on the real wiring and transferred to nulls (P1), each wiring tuned on its own (P2), and P2 restricted to physiology consistent with independent data (P3). The biases involved are known in machine learning (under-tuned baselines, inherited weights, winner's curse); we measure what they do to biological conclusions, using synthetic ground truth, placebo nulls and three Drosophila circuit models. Some claims survive every protocol we test: segregated reward and punishment dopamine improves learning, and head-direction topography is required for a persistent bump. Others do not. In the mushroom body, the real Kenyon-cell output wiring beats a cross-subtype identity shuffle by 0.09 under P1 and P2 but loses to it by 0.09 under P3 (95% CIs exclude zero; held-out runs confirm). The verdict is set by the share of alpha'beta' cells among active Kenyon cells, which P1 selects low; at the share implied by imaging (about 44%) the real-wiring model fails to learn, exposing a model inadequacy rather than a deficit of the fly's wiring. In flyvis, P1 penalises a mirrored connectome, which has a constructed solution within 0.07 (median) of the real error, more than a spatially shuffled one in 50 of 50 members; the ranking survives ten-fold longer retraining but depends on the checkpoint at fifty-fold. A credible structural claim needs matched optimisation, data-constrained physiology and a model that still works there.

articles.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
articles.content: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. The same tasks return after dormant gaps with fresh instances, while new tasks keep arriving. On each instance, the learner may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act inside the harness, with retries permitted on incorrect submissions, which are paid for. Each instance is scored based on the share of this feedback budget consumed. Since a learner may keep anything between instances, memory-based and weight-based systems are scored on the same scale. After the stream, the learner is frozen and tested on fresh instances of the tasks it met, which measures memorization, and on unseen tasks, which measures generalization. We run an agent harness with frozen weights, with and without persistence, on Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-5.3 Flash, comparing them with two prompting floors, a program-induction method and Qwen3.5-9B's weights trained to imitate GLM-5.3 Flash. Persistence in the harness generally does not improve memorization unless provided with explicit expert guidance. Most harness-based methods still learn less than a floor that simply caches each task's demonstrations, across all models we tested. No harness-based method gains on unseen tasks, whereas weight-based learning shows substantial gains. This opens the door to future weight-based continual learning that could teach models to drive harnesses in new domains.

articles.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
articles.content: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly. This demonstrates that loss-based scaling laws alone are insufficient to predict when zero-shot emergent capabilities become available. The capabilities reported here emerge after training at a 1:2,000 parameter-to-token ratio to accommodate the sparsity of paired biological interaction data. The same frozen representations achieve state-of-the-art binding and affinity prediction at five orders of magnitude greater speed than co-folding methods. In prospective wet-lab validation across nine disease targets spanning seven protein families, Bonbon achieves a 61.5% dose-response hit rate on de novo compounds, yielding structurally novel molecules not previously reported to inhibit these proteins, including for out-of-distribution targets.

articles.title: Measuring Robustness and Efficiency in a Connectome-Constrained Fly Visual System Model: Linking an Adversarial and a Perceptual Illusion
articles.content: Biological visual systems compute reliably under tight metabolic and wiring constraints, whereas artificial vision systems consume far more energy and can be sensitive to adversarial perturbations. Whether networks with brain-like wiring are more robust at lower computational cost is unclear. We address this by benchmarking a task-optimized, continuous-time recurrent neural network of the fly visual system constrained by its synaptic connectome (FlyNet) against artificial neural networks. We compare it against CNNs, RAFT, and continuous-time recurrent neural networks without detailed connectome constraints (sCTRNN, CTRNN) on a collision-detection task within a differentiable 3D rendering pipeline. FlyNet is adversarially vulnerable but, relative to its compute, more robust to common video corruptions than RAFT, while using up to five orders of magnitude fewer FLOPs. The CTRNNs remain more robust than FlyNet across almost all tested perturbations, suggesting that connectome constraints benefit efficiency, through their low edge count, over robustness. Recurrence improves robustness to white-box attacks in RAFT and temporal context improves robustness to common corruptions. FlyNet's position and velocity representations degrade under adversarial textures but recover under counterfactual textures that restore correct classification while staying equally far from training, ruling out unfamiliar textures as the cause of failure. The reverse-phi illusion similarly disrupts these representations and inverts the same low-level motion statistic as the adversarial textures. Optimizing this input statistic alone, without access to the network, suffices to induce classification failure, attributing both perturbations to the same circuit vulnerability. Connectome-constrained models can thus surface adversarial failure mechanisms as testable hypotheses about biological perceptual vulnerabilities.

articles.title: RS-JEPA: Remote Sensing Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with Scan-Path Views for Cross-Sensor Image Retrieval
articles.content: Cross-sensor remote sensing image retrieval aims to find scenes with the same content across heterogeneous sensors, such as SAR and optical or panchromatic (PAN) and multispectral (MS) imagery, without manual labels. Existing self-supervised methods either reconstruct sensor-specific pixel detail, align each image only with its co-registered twin, or rely on large transformers with 118-173M parameters (and up to 398M). We introduce RS-JEPA, a compact joint-embedding predictive framework built on a Vision Mamba encoder shared by both sensors. Since a state-space encoder reads an image as an ordered sequence of patches, we propose scan-path views, which treat two reading orders of the same image as two views with identical pixels and predict the hidden patches in one order from the visible patches in the other.To keep this prediction challenging, we propose Adversarial View Coupling (AVC), which learns the hardest split of the visible patches, and a neighbourhood consensus loss that aligns the scene similarities of both sensors. Extensive experiments on SAR-optical (BEN-14K, CBRSIR-VS) and PAN-MS (DSRSID) benchmarks demonstrate that RS-JEPA achieves the highest F1@5 among twelve re-implemented methods (72.92, 80.35 and 94.43) with a retrieval network of only 3.88M parameters (14.57M in training, 8-16times fewer than prior JEPA retrievers). Like prior methods, RS-JEPA trains on co-registered pairs. Our results highlight reading order as a source of self-supervised views. code: https://github.com/Tanishq251/RSJEPA.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
articles.content: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. We present a three-phase comparative study of three evaluation frameworks, each representing a distinct evaluation paradigm (trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics), applied to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting using frozen execution traces. Phase 1 quantifies evaluation harness stability through repeated measurements, finding that 97% of configurations meet the stability threshold and that stability patterns are agent-independent. Phase 2 measures known risk detection on 72 ground-truth test cases, where the trace-based framework achieves the best precision-recall balance (F1=0.90) while text-only evaluation matches on recall but generates 5x more false alarms. Phase 3 evaluates unknown risk discovery, uncovering 24 novel failures with zero overlap between functional testing and security red-teaming. Our results demonstrate that (1) the information available to the evaluation harness determines evaluation quality, (2) functional and security evaluation are complementary, and (3) LLM-based evaluation harnesses surface subtle errors that human reviewers miss. We recommend a two-framework strategy: trace-based evaluation for functional assessment and adversarial red-teaming for security validation.

articles.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
articles.content: Business process automation runs the same Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) again and again on new inputs. Large Language Model (LLM) agents can follow an SOP written in natural language, but they call an LLM to choose every step of every run, which adds latency and cost at scale. We present ReTrace, which turns an SOP and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow in which code, not an LLM, selects the next step. The agent's reasoning, the explanation it writes with each tool call, often states why it took an action; the tool calls alone do not. ReTrace extracts the condition behind each step, merges these conditions across runs into a compact rule document, and generates an executable workflow from it. Only this last stage depends on the platform, so rule documents can be compiled for different orchestration platforms. On $79$ procedures from our production platform, ReTrace workflows reach $93.8\%$ completion, against $96.8\%$ for the agent, at $24\%$ lower cost per task. On $τ^2$-Bench, they reach $75.8\%$ task success (agent: $80.6\%$) and run in $1.3$s instead of $170$s; three rounds of repair on training failures lift $k{=}2$ workflows from $66.7\%$ to $81.2\%$. On eight SOP-Bench procedures, ReTrace without repair trails few-shot generation ($80.6\%$ vs. $83.6\%$), but repair from labeled training failures lifts it to $87.8\%$ at $0.40$s per task, compared to $85.5\%$ in $46.6$s for the agent.

articles.title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
articles.content: Time series analytics has been widely applied across various domains. While existing time series foundation models (TSFMs) have demonstrated promising results, they still face two major challenges: 1) Most TSFMs mainly rely on stacking Transformer layers to increase parameter size, lacking the ability to adaptively model complex time series patterns from multi-domain data. 2) Current TSFMs are primarily pre-trained for specific tasks, e.g., forecasting or anomaly detection, and a few models support multiple tasks, but they fail to fully leverage task specificity and commonality, resulting in suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose TimeSeek, a novel generalized time series analytics model that adaptively models time series patterns from multi-domain data and unifies multiple tasks in pre-training. Conceptually, TimeSeek is guided by selective information sharing under domain and task heterogeneity. From the perspective of multi-domain data, we propose a Multi-Domain Feature Extractor that adaptively captures temporal dependencies and channel correlations based on domain-specific characteristics, including progressive multi-scale modeling and adaptive slot channel modeling. From the perspective of the diversity of tasks, we propose multi-task collaborative training, which leverages task specificity and task commonality through task customization and cross-task training, effectively unifying multiple tasks in pre-training and better adapting to diverse downstream scenarios. After pre-training on large-scale time series data, TimeSeek achieves state-of-the-art performance in forecasting, anomaly detection, and classification tasks across both few-shot learning and zero-shot situations, together with favorable inference efficiency.

articles.title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
articles.content: Memory-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) policies are meant to remember what happened. Many of them, however, fill memory by time: they sample frames uniformly across the episode and stamp each frame with its time step. Because time passes even when nothing happens, such a memory may not tell waiting from working. We show that it does not. On the counting tasks of RoboMME, we make the robot briefly pause or fidget its wrist. Such a null event changes nothing the task depends on, yet a released memory VLA counts the interval as work done and stops early. We call this failure phantom progress. It cuts success from 47 to 16 of 50 on one task and from 44 to 10 on the other. When the same frames are withheld from memory, success returns, so the cause lies in memory rather than in the interruption itself. We trace the failure to a temporal shortcut: because demonstrations proceed at a steady pace, elapsed time predicts progress. Indeed, rescaling the time stamps alone makes the policy stop early when the clock runs fast and repeat when it runs slow. Surprisingly, removing the time encoding does not cure the failure, because the frames of a null event still occupy slots of the time-sampled memory. Across RoboMME's released designs, vulnerability follows how memory is indexed. Of the fixes the diagnosis suggests, training with injected pauses does not remove the failure and impairs counting, whereas indexing memory by events recovers half or more of the loss without retraining. A memory meant to remember what happened should count events rather than clock ticks.

articles.title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
articles.content: Research ideation is iterative: researchers refine their ideas step by step based on feedback. Yet existing evaluations obscure this search process, making it difficult to understand how LLMs explore the space of research ideas and what limits their progress. We introduce Re-Search, which adapts the format of Twenty Questions to research ideation: given only the research problem of a published paper, a model must rediscover the paper's core idea by asking yes-or-no questions. Built from 200 ICML 2026 papers, Re-Search tracks how a model's idea evolves as it asks questions and receives binary oracle feedback, isolating ideation from execution. Across six recent LLMs, nearly all progress happens within the first 30 of 100 questions, which largely decide how the game ends; after that, most models plateau. Through controlled interventions on the candidate questions and the hypothesis space, we find that the bottleneck is generation, not judgment: models recognize a good idea or a good question when one is offered, but often cannot produce it on their own. We further analyze the ideation traces and find that models fail by either over-exploiting one direction or over-exploring too many. These findings point to concrete design principles for autoresearch systems: since models can judge candidates they cannot produce, enriching the search with externally sourced ideas and questions may be more effective than improving any single model's generation ability.

articles.title: Mechanistic Interpretability Needs a Logic of Inference
articles.content: Neural networks are increasingly studied not merely as predictive systems, but as complex systems whose internal computations are themselves objects of scientific inquiry. Recent progress in mechanistic interpretability (MI) has made it possible to identify neurons, features, circuits, population structures, and dynamical patterns associated with model behavior. As these tools improve, attention is shifting from what can be observed inside a model to how those observations support mechanistic explanations. We examine the parallel efforts of neuroscience and MI to address this question and identify recurring inferential bottlenecks when inferring mechanisms from complex neural systems. We propose five principles and organize them into a recursive logic for a more rigorous procedure of mechanistic inference. These principles provide a framework that supports scientific discovery in two senses: it helps turn local interpretability findings into cumulative knowledge of mechanisms within models, and it makes those mechanisms sufficiently precise to generate testable hypotheses about domains beyond the models. Evidence beyond MI is ultimately required to establish what model mechanisms reveal about the world.

articles.content: In this paper, we present 1020 Group's submission to the WMT26 shared task on automated quality evaluation. Our system, Pterodactyl, was engineered specifically for subtasks 2 and 3, that is, segment-level quality score prediction and the detection of error-free segments. Pterodactyl is a highly customizable, ultra-low cost system optimized for binary classification in translation triage and data curation. It is based on an LLM-as-a-judge approach, with prompt engineering and model selection guided by ROC analysis. We also developed several variants of Pterodactyl that were specifically adapted for subtasks 3.

articles.title: FERN: Cross-Benchmark Table Retrieval for Text-to-SQL with Frozen Retrievers and Learned Ranking
articles.content: Text-to-SQL systems over large pooled catalogs must first retrieve the tables a question needs. We compare against the published table recall of RASL, which uses Claude 3.5 models to extract keywords and select tables, on pooled BIRD, Spider, and Fiben catalogs. FERN (Feature-Engineered Ranking with No generative LLM) instead fuses three frozen retrievers into 100 candidates, describes each with up to 120 features, and reorders them with LightGBM rankers fitted once on BIRD's training questions. On Spider, where it was not fitted, its candidate pool alone reaches RASL's published recall at fifteen tables (98.0), and the ranker raises the share of questions with every gold table in the top five (complete@5) from 83.9% to 95.6%. At five tables, FERN's recall is within one point of RASL's on Spider (96.7 vs 97.0) and on BIRD with its evidence hints (96.6 vs 97.5), and 8.2 points below on BIRD without them (89.3). On 121 real BEAVER questions, without BEAVER fitting, its recall at fifteen (82.1) falls between two BEAVER-trained retrievers (80.8, 84.5), but its complete@15 is below both (49.6 vs 54.5 and 62.0). On Fiben, it falls far short at fifteen tables (54.2 vs 69.2, different question sets), although its recall at fifty is numerically close to RASL's question-only retrieval result (80.7 vs 79.4). On BIRD dev with evidence, non-retrieval features raise complete@5 by 7.7 points over retrieval signals alone. On BIRD dev, median latency is 208 ms per question on one A100, without hosted model calls.
